package_info.package_manager: custom/third-party JavaScript (not npm, but included as a static asset)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because attackers injected unauthorized JavaScript code at the end of the widely used modernizr library. This modification transformed the library into a skimmer that harvested payment form data, including credit card details, and exfiltrated it to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The injected code was not present in the legitimate modernizr release and enabled large-scale compromise of sensitive user data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user loads and interacts with the payment form in their browser
execution_context.file_location: modernizr.js (malicious code appended to the end of the legitimate library, served as a static asset on the website)
required_permissions: DOM access (to read form fields and attach event listeners)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches a submit event listener to the payment form, collects all form data (including sensitive payment details) upon submission, and sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled external domain, resulting in exfiltration of user credentials and payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it intercepts all data entered into the payment form and transmits it to an external domain that is not associated with the legitimate business, enabling theft of sensitive information such as credit card numbers and personal details.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate JavaScript library like modernizr is only expected to perform feature detection and should never access payment forms or transmit user data to third-party domains. The presence of code that manipulates form submissions and sends data externally is a clear violation of expected behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and typically with user consent and visible privacy disclosures. They do not silently exfiltrate sensitive data to unknown or untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Malicious code appended to a widely used third-party library (modernizr.js)
Event listener attached to payment form submission events
Collection of all form data, including sensitive fields, using FormData API
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to an attacker-controlled, non-canonical domain
Use of fetch or XMLHttpRequest to transmit user input outside the expected business infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits an unpatched Magento installation to gain unauthorized access to the web server hosting the website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify static assets, including JavaScript libraries, served to users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker appends malicious JavaScript skimming code to the end of the modernizr.js library file.
attack_chain.leads_to: The compromised modernizr.js is served to all users visiting the payment page, embedding the malicious code in their browsers.

attack_chain.action: When a user loads the payment page, the malicious code executes in their browser, intercepts payment form submissions, and exfiltrates the captured data to the attacker's external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credit card and personal data from victims, enabling large-scale data theft.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in static assets that attaches event listeners to payment or checkout forms
Outbound network requests from payment pages to untrusted or unexpected external domains
Unexpected modifications or appended code in third-party libraries such as modernizr.js
file_indicators: modernizr.js file with appended or altered code not present in the official modernizr release
Static asset files (e.g., modernizr.js) with recent unauthorized changes or mismatched hashes compared to known-good versions
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers on payment or checkout pages to domains not associated with the legitimate business (e.g., malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual or unauthorized outbound traffic from payment pages to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor static assets for unauthorized changes by comparing deployed files to known-good cryptographic hashes. Inspect JavaScript on payment and checkout pages for event listeners on forms that send data to external domains. Enforce and monitor Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict outbound requests from sensitive pages. Analyze network traffic for POST requests to unknown or untrusted domains originating from payment or checkout pages, and alert on deviations from expected domain lists.
